editorial:
You step into a strange future where ads and logos feel like living things, and one man starts pulling at the threads of a massive corporate plot. The story follows Misha, an ad guy who gets pulled into a world where brands are more than just products. It has a weird, dark mood that keeps you curious, even when things get confusing. The visuals are bold and the city feels cold and busy, so you always feel like something is hiding around the corner.

The acting is solid, and the movie has some cool ideas about how marketing controls people. The pacing can be slow in spots, and the plot gets messy near the end, but it still gives you plenty to talk about. If you like odd sci-fi thrillers with a message, this is worth a look. Stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent it on Apple TV, or grab the 4K Blu-ray if you want the best picture.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, Misha learns the brands are actually living monsters feeding on human desire. He fights back and exposes the truth, breaking the spell that made people worship products. The twist is that the conspiracy was bigger than one company, and the ending leaves you wondering if people can ever fully escape the pull of advertising.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves odd sci-fi thrillers with a message.
